messages.subject: Latent Means - MGCFA - categorical variables - loadings
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I have a question regarding the case of MGCFA with ordered categorical variables. 

I would like to know if the interpretation of the latent means (the intercepts for the latent variables) is the same that with continuous variables? 
I have two groups (the first: France and the second: Germany).

The model that I use is :

model2.new<-'range = ~ NA*gvjbevn + gvhlthc + gvslvol + gvslvue + gvcldcr + gvpdlwk
goals = ~ NA*sbprvpv + sbeqsoc + sbcwkfm
range~~1*range
goals~~1*goals
gvhlthc ~~ gvslvol
gvcldcr ~~ gvpdlwk
gvcldcr~*~c(1,1)*gvcldcr
gvslvol~*~c(1,1)*gvslvol
sbeqsoc~*~c(1,1)*sbeqsoc
'

gvjbevn, gvhlthc, gvslvol, gvslvue, gvcldcr and gvpdlwk go to 0 to 10 (0: Not governments' responsibility at all to 10:Entirely governments' responsibility) 
sbprvpv, sbeqsoc and sbcwkfm go to 1 to 5 (1:Agree strongly to 5:Disagree strongly)

I have the partial equivalence with 
model.cfa.group.loadings.thre<-cfa(model2.new,ordered=varcat,data=sub,estimator="WLSMV"
                                   ,group="cntry",group.equal = c("loadings", "thresholds")
                                   ,group.partial = c("range=~gvcldcr","gvcldcr|t1","gvcldcr|t2","gvcldcr|t3","gvcldcr|t4","gvcldcr|t5","gvcldcr|t6","gvcldcr|t7","gvcldcr|t8","gvcldcr|t9","gvcldcr|t10"
,"range=~ gvslvol","gvslvol|t1","gvslvol|t2","gvslvol|t3","gvslvol|t4","gvslvol|t5","gvslvol|t6","gvslvol|t7","gvslvol|t8","gvslvol|t9","gvslvol|t10"
,"goals=~ sbeqsoc","sbeqsoc|t1","sbeqsoc|t2","sbeqsoc|t3","sbeqsoc|t4"))


I would like to know how I can interpret the latent means! I attached the screen shots of my R-output (just the latent variables, covariances and the intercepts).

Thank you in advance for your help.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Latent Means - MGCFA - categorical variables - loadings
parts: I would like to know if the interpretation of the latent means (the intercepts for the latent variables) is the same that with continuous variables?

Which latent variables?  With continuous indicator variables, you model latent common factors and a latent unique factor (with mean fixed to zero) for each indicator.  When you have ordered categorical indicators, you add a third set of latent variables to the model: a latent item-response (assumed to be normally distributed, with mean fixed to zero) underlying each observed item.  The common factors are assumed to be normally distributed, regardless of the distribution of the observed indicators, so the interpretation of common-factor means does not depend on the distribution of your indicators.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Latent Means - MGCFA - categorical variables - loadings
parts: The intercepts of my categorical variable are fixed to 0 for the two groups. However, the intercepts for the two latents variables are fixed to 0 for the first group but for the second group the intercepts are not equal to 0. If I am not wrong these values are the latent means. And I don't know how I can interpret these values

The same way you would if your items were continuous.  Since there is no implicit scale to the latent variables (because we haven't observed them), it only makes sense to compare them across groups.  So a latent mean difference between groups would be meaningful to interpret.  Because the Group-1 means are already fixed to zero, Mean_g2 - Mean_g1 == Mean_g2 - 0 == Mean_g2 (i.e., you can interpret the Group-2 latent means as a mean-difference compared to Group 1).  If the latent variances in both Groups are 1, they are also standardized latent mean differences (i.e., Cohen's d).  If not, you can either calculate the pooled SD across groups to calculate Cohen's d yourself, or if you can consider Group 1 a control group (or otherwise meaningful reference group), you could interpret the estimated Group-2 mean as a Glass' delta because Group-1's latent SD is already fixed to 1.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Hello,

I’ve also got a question concerning the handling and interpretation of latent means in lavaan. I’ve specified a 3-wave cross-lagged panel model with 2 latent constructs, each defined though 4 ordinal indicators (4-point Likert scale).

 

Here is my syntax:

 

model1<- '

Y1 =~ y11 + a*y12 + b*y13 + c*y14

Y2 =~ y21 + a*y22 + b*y23 + c*y24

Y3 =~ y31 + a*y32 + b*y33 + c*y34

 

X1 =~ x11 + a*x12 + b*x13 + c*x14

X2 =~ x21 + a*x22 + b*x23 + c*x24

X3 =~ x31 + a*x32 + b*x33 + c*x34

 

Y1 ~ 0*1

Y2 ~ 1

Y3 ~ 1

 

X1 ~ 0*1

X2 ~ 1

X3 ~ 1

 

 

Y2 ~ Y1 + X1

Y3 ~ Y2 + X2

X2 ~ X1 + Y1

X3 ~ X2 + Y2

 

X2 ~~ Y2

 

y11 | tau11*t1 + tau12*t2 + tau13*t3

y21 | tau11*t1 + tau12*t2 + tau13*t3

y31 | tau11*t1 + tau12*t2 + tau13*t3

 

… etc. (for each item of both Y and X thresholds are constrained to be equal across time; omitted here to save space)

 

y11~~y21+y31

y21~~y31

 

… etc. (autocorrelated residual structure for both Y and X; omitted here to save space)

'

fit1 <- sem(model1, data=demo, ordered= cvar, parameterization="theta", estimator="WLSMV", missing="pairwise")

summary(fit1, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

 

I’ve got some trouble with the interpretation of the latent means, because as far as I know, WLSMV with theta-parameterization produces probit estimates. I’m not sure how to handle these probit estimates.


(1)  Are the latent means also probit estimates, i.e. z-scores? Thus, how would I interpret the latent means relating to the reference occasion? I’ve got difficulties to interpret the recent answers referring to the probit estimates.


(2) Following Newsom (2015), the factor mean estimates may be transformed into proportions of the number choosing the first response category using the normal cumulative distribution function. How would I calculate this in lavaan or R, respectively? And according to this how can I calculate in a similar manner, for example, the proportions of the number endorsing the two highest categories?


(3) How can I plot the latent means for both constructs Y and X on the basis of the lavaan output?


Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Latent Means - MGCFA - categorical variables - loadings
parts: (1)  Are the latent means also probit estimates, i.e. z-scores?

No, the probit link is only applied to ordinal outcomes (your indicators).  The common factors are assumed to be normally distributed (and are modeled that way), so you interpret your latent regression paths as linear slopes.
how would I interpret the latent means relating to the reference occasion?

You don't have latent mean estimates.  The later time points are endogenous, conditional on previous time points.  So Y2 ~ 1 is an intercept, which is the mean of Y2 conditional on the predictors (Y1 & X1) being zero.  Since the latent means are zero at Time 1, then the intercept of Y2 is the mean of Y2 among people with means on Y1 and X1 (likewise for the intercept of X2).  The intercept of Y3 would be interpreted the same way, except the means of Y2 and X2 are not necessarily zero.  But the intercept is still the mean of the outcome when its predictors == 0.

(2) Following Newsom (2015), the factor mean estimates may be transformed into proportions of the number choosing the first response category using the normal cumulative distribution function. How would I calculate this in lavaan or R, respectively? And according to this how can I calculate in a similar manner, for example, the proportions of the number endorsing the two highest categories?

Are you talking about common factor means (which are normally distributed variables) or latent item response means/intercepts (which are the normally distributed variables assumed to underlie the observed ordinal response)?  I don't know what the formula is, but if you have it in front of you, you can calculate it from the parameter estimates in the output.

params <- lavInspect(fit1, "coef")
params$tau                  # thresholds
params$alpha                # latent intercepts
lavInspect(fit1, "mean.ov") # model-implied means of latent item responses
lavInspect(fit1, "mean.lv") # model-implied means of latent common factors

The normal CDF is the pnorm() function.  If you provide a vector of quantiles (e.g., thresholds) in a normal distribution with specified mean and sd, it will return the cumulative (left-tail) probabilities.
(3) How can I plot the latent means for both constructs Y and X on the basis of the lavaan output?

Create a vector of X means and plot them, then add the line for Y means.  Here's an example that should work:

M <- lavInspect(fit1, "mean.lv")
plot(M[paste0("X", 1:3)], type = "l", col = "red", lwd = 2, main = "Latent Means",
      xlab = "Occasion", ylab = "Mean", ylim = range(M))
lines(M[paste0("Y", 1:3)], col = "blue", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("X","Y"), col = c("blue","red"), lwd = c(2, 2))

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
